problem: Prior language-guided navigation methods (Seq2Seq/CMA imitation or RL) make single-step greedy decisions from local RGB-D observations, accumulating errors and generalizing poorly to unseen environments. Map-based works build noisy 2D maps on the fly and treat them as extra visual input, so they do not exploit global map information.
motivation: In many deployments (home or hotel robots) the environment is static and can be pre-scanned into a 3D semantic map. A map gives global information for planning whole trajectories and shares semantic definitions across environments, which should help generalization. Decoupling map construction from map navigation also gives a clean benchmark for language-guided navigation algorithms.
key_idea: Propose instruction-aware candidate paths on a 3D semantic map with A* constrained by extracted landmarks and turn actions, then score them with a transformer discriminator over object-compass path features and the instruction.
insight: Most of the gain comes from combining the two stages. Uniform sampling from the proposal pool gets 20.3% SR (unseen) versus 4.0% for random paths, and the discriminator lifts it to 38.0%. Semantic object-compass features matter most: removing them drops SR by 16 points (seen) and 13 points (unseen), while removing agent pose costs only ~2 points. Map-based models show a smaller seen-unseen gap (5.7 SR points for iPPD) than RGB-D VLN-CE models (e.g. 11.9 for HPN).
method: Key component extraction: POS tagging, Lesk WSD and WuPalmer similarity (threshold 0.85) map nouns to one of 40 object labels; rule-based pattern matching extracts 'turn left/right' actions.

Instruction-aware path proposal: A* paths from the start visit the key components in order and end near the last landmark. Pruning drops paths that violate turn actions, cap the search at 5 m per landmark, and merge same-label objects by DBSCAN (0.5 m), for an overall reduction of 85% from ~560 average candidates. Random A* paths within 20 m are the fallback.

Path feature encoding: each path is discretized into key points. An object compass (objects within 3 m in egocentric coordinates, GloVe-50 class embeddings) is encoded by PointNet. Agent pose (position and orientation) gets NeRF-style positional encoding and an FFN.

Language-driven discriminator: a 6-layer, 12-head transformer takes [CLS], GloVe-embedded instruction tokens and the path features, and outputs a path score from the [CLS] token; the highest-scoring path is the prediction.

Training objective: MSE regression to a target score, a λ-weighted mix of nDTW with the GT path and endpoint distance term, plus a masked language modeling loss (15% masking). Trained with AdamW at lr 1e-4 on one P100 for 12 h.
Semantic map construction: Matterport3D semantic meshes are interpolated to point clouds and voxelized at 0.05 m with instance and category labels (40 categories) and NavMesh-derived navigability.

setting.backbone: 6-layer 12-head transformer + PointNet + GloVe + FFNs (trained from scratch); rule-based/A* proposal
setting.training_data: VLN-CE (R2R v1_2) train split with self-built 3D semantic maps on single-floor Matterport3D environments; no extra data
setting.observation: 3D voxelized semantic map (object category and navigable labels) plus instruction; no RGB-D
setting.action_space: whole-path selection among A*-planned candidate paths on the voxel map
setting.simulator: Matterport3D-based semantic maps (VLN-CE / Habitat dataset), no online simulation
setting.privileged: Complete ground-truth 3D semantic map of the environment (GT semantic labels and NavMesh navigability); start pose given

numbers.eval_set_note: VLN-CE val-unseen episodes on single-floor environments (map-language navigation variant, semantic maps instead of RGB-D)
numbers.extra: Uses GT 3D semantic map; task differs from standard VLN-CE (no RGB-D)

numbers.eval_set_note: VLN-CE val-seen episodes on single-floor environments (map-language navigation variant)
numbers.extra: Uses GT 3D semantic map; task differs from standard VLN-CE

numbers_note: Metrics printed as fractions (0.380 etc.), copied as printed. The task is a new map-language navigation benchmark built from VLN-CE, so numbers are not comparable with standard R2R-CE. Baselines Seq2Seq-MAP and CMA-MAP are excluded.
results: On the new map-language navigation task, iPPD reaches 38.0% SR and 0.604 nDTW on unseen environments, versus Seq2Seq-MAP (20.9% SR, 0.416 nDTW) and CMA-MAP (18.4% SR, 0.412 nDTW), gaining about 17 and 20 SR points. It also has a smaller seen-to-unseen gap than RGB-D VLN-CE models and beats the reproduced HPN+DN on unseen SR (0.380 vs 0.363), though the tasks and splits differ.
limitations: Assumes a static, pre-scanned perfect semantic map; dynamic objects and obstacle avoidance are not handled.
Assumes instructions follow the shortest path, so instructions requiring detours may not be covered by the proposals; keyword extraction covers only landmarks plus left/right turns.
Evaluated only on single-floor Matterport environments with a self-built benchmark, and the HPN comparison is not on identical data.
